title: Pilot: cryptographically-signed, verifiable security attestations for SIG/CAIQ responses
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Problem: Enterprise procurement and legal teams increasingly ask for attestations that are auditable and tamper-evident. Current SIG/CAIQ PDFs and email answers are manually produced and hard to verify programmatically. Goal: prototype a hybrid self-serve + concierge attestation flow that issues cryptographically-signed attestations (verifiable credential style) tied to a CAIQ answer set and evidence artifacts. These attestations can be timestamped, revoked, and surfaced in contract handoffs to reduce negotiation cycles and manual evidence requests. This ticket scopes a 6-week pilot focused on: 1) data model for signed attestations and minimal evidence links, 2) signer service design (HSM/KMS integration), 3) UI for requesting/issuing an attestation in Console, and 4) experiment matrix for pricing/packaging and SLA (time-to-issue) options.

acceptance_criteria: PoC signer service can produce verifiable, timestamped signatures for a JSON CAIQ answer export
Console flow to request an attestation exists in a gated Enterprise settings area (mocked UX allowed)
Attestation objects include signer metadata, issuance timestamp, TTL/revocation pointer, and a link to source evidence artifacts (S3/Drive) in read-only mode
Legal-approved attestation wording is embedded and stored with the attestation; revocation and rotation policies documented
Pilot experiment plan with two pricing variants and measurable success metrics defined
rollout_plan: Week 1 (pilot build): implement signer PoC, define JSON attestation schema, add basic audit log events
Week 2 (integration): KMS integration (dev/test), Console UI mock, legal wording finalized
Week 3 (internal trial): issue 10 internal attestations, validate verification flow (crypto verify), run manual revocation test
Week 4 (customer pilot): invite 3 enterprise customers from sales pipeline; measure SLA, support tickets, and contract negotiation time
Post-pilot: evaluate metrics, decision whether to generalize to self-serve or keep as concierge add-on
metrics: Primary: reduction in enterprise contract negotiation time (days) for pilots vs baseline
Primary: percent of customers able to accept attestation without supplemental evidence requests
Secondary: time-to-issue attestation (hours), support tickets created per attestation
Secondary: revocation/rotation incidents and audit log coverage
artifacts: Legal draft: Drive > Security > Attestations > wording-draft-v1.docx
risks: Regulatory: Certain customers may require signatures that need HSM-backed key ceremony; our MVP KMS approach may not be acceptable
Operational: Key rotation and revocation complexity could increase support load if not automated
Product: Customers may request fine-grained per-answer evidence rather than a single attest blob, increasing integration cost
Security: Signed attestations create a stronger trust surface; must ensure signing keys and audit trails are fully protected
